body.text: Detailed Analysis of Recent Appellate Jurisprudence
1. Tuna Temple Inc. v. Canada, 2026 FCA 175 (Decided October 21, 2026)

In the most recent Federal Court of Appeal decision on SR&ED eligibility, the Court upheld the Tax Court of Canada's dismissal (2025 TCC 183) of Tuna Temple Inc.'s appeal concerning 13 of 14 R&D projects claimed across its 2005 through 2009 taxation years. At the Tax Court trial, the judge accepted that the company's witness was credible, and the Crown called no competing witnesses of its own. On appeal, Tuna Temple argued that its credible, uncontradicted witness testimony adequately described the project methodology and technological uncertainty and should have been sufficient to overturn the reassessments.

The Federal Court of Appeal dismissed the appeal with costs, establishing four vital litigation and audit principles. First, to overturn the Tax Court's factual determinations on the five Northwest Hydraulic criteria, an appellant must establish a "palpable and overriding error". Second, the Court drew a sharp legal distinction between witness credibility and proof of statutory eligibility: finding a witness honest and credible does not mean their testimony satisfies the legal requirements of subsection 248(1) or substitutes for objective evidence addressing the Minister's assumptions. Third, for each of the 13 disallowed projects, the Tax Court properly found factual deficiencies across the five criteria—specifically, the absence of a scientific hypothesis, reliance on existing technology rather than seeking technological advancement, the use of a trial-and-error method rather than a systematic investigation, inadequate project records, and failure to establish a gap in existing industry knowledge. Fourth, the Court confirmed that the Crown is not required to call contradictory witnesses and may rely on the taxpayer's existing documents, witness statements, and cross-examination to sustain the assessment.
2. National R & D Inc. v. The Queen, 2020 TCC 47 (Decided July 7, 2020)

In National R & D Inc., an engineering and SR&ED consulting corporation appealed the disallowance of $68,029 in SR&ED expenditures (and $23,810 in ITCs) for its 2011 taxation year relating to the development of a web-based Project Tracking System ("PTS Project") built to automate filing SR&ED claims. The company's president and sole witness (accepted as a litigant expert) testified that the project used a multi-tiered architecture comprising ADO, Classic ASP, COM+, and Microsoft SQL Server 2000, and sought to develop record-set paging, sorting, and in-memory array pivoting ("pivot-like output"). Crucially, the company chose not to upgrade to Microsoft SQL Server 2005—which already possessed built-in PIVOT commands—due to financial constraints and employee familiarity with legacy tools.

Justice Dominique Lafleur dismissed the appeal with costs, establishing two major precedents for software and IT SR&ED claims. First, under Criterion 1 (Technological Uncertainty), the Court held that self-imposed financial or tool constraints—such as electing to use legacy SQL Server 2000 instead of upgrading to SQL Server 2005—and relying on publicly available internet articles on SQL paging and pivoting do not constitute genuine technological uncertainty that cannot be resolved by routine engineering or standard procedures. Second, under Criterion 3 (Scientific Method) and Criterion 5 (Contemporaneous Records), the Court held that while oral testimony is admissible under RIS-Christie and Formadrain, establishing systematic scientific research requires documentary evidence demonstrating a logical progression between successive tests; a high-level project timeline containing vague descriptions of work completed and time entries without recording how hypotheses were tested or modified, or what measurable results were obtained, is fatal to the claim. The Federal Court of Appeal dismissed National's appeal (National R&D Inc. v. Canada, 2022 FCA 72, May 3, 2022), and the Supreme Court of Canada dismissed the application for leave to appeal (Docket 40303).
9. Comprehensive Audit Compliance Checklist for Canadian Claimants

To ensure full compliance with the post-Bill C-15 statutory regime and current CRA audit standards in 2026, corporate tax directors and R&D leaders should execute the following ten-point audit protocol before filing Form T661:

items: Evaluate Pre-Claim Approval Eligibility Before Project Kickoff: If annual gross business income is under $25 million, consider submitting an optional Form T1322 Pre-Claim Approval application via My Business Account for up to 3 proposed projects to secure an 8-week upfront technical determination, 3-year eligibility certainty, and a 90-day fast-track expenditure review.

Isolate Technological Uncertainty from Business Objectives: Before drafting Part 2 of Form T661, state the specific scientific or technological uncertainty in a single sentence explaining why standard engineering or publicly available knowledge could not achieve the objective, and document the sequential hypotheses, experimental logs, failed trials, and quantitative results contemporaneously.

Model the $6M Expenditure Limit Phase-Out (Taxable Capital vs. Gross Revenue Election): For CCPCs with prior-year associated taxable capital approaching or exceeding $15 million, model whether electing the 3-year average gross revenue phase-out under subsections 127(10.31) or 127(10.32) preserves a larger portion of the $6,000,000 enhanced 35% expenditure limit. Ensure associated CCPC allocations on Schedule T2SCH49 (or consolidated ECPC allocations under subsection 127(10.62)) are filed on time.

Perform an Annual Arithmetic Comparison of the Proxy (55%) vs. Traditional Method: Never default blindly to the proxy method. Calculate 55% of the restricted salary base under Regulation 2900(4) (excluding bonuses, taxable benefits, and unpaid wages, and applying the 75% and 2.5x YMPE = $186,500 cap for specified employees in 2026) and compare it against actual, directly related, and incremental overhead—especially where cloud computing (AWS/Azure/GCP), leased bandwidth, or utility costs exceed 55% of the salary base.

Audit Specified Employee Caps and File Form T1174: Verify all 10%+ shareholders and non-arm's length relatives on payroll. Strip 100% of their bonuses and profit-based remuneration, enforce the $373,000 (5x YMPE in 2026) direct wage cap under subsection 37(9.1) and the $186,500 (2.5x YMPE in 2026) proxy base cap under Regulation 2900(7), and file Form T1174 if any specified employee worked for multiple associated corporations.

Maintain Contemporaneous Operating-Time Logs for Post-December 15, 2024 Capital and Leased Equipment: To substantiate restored capital expenditures (Line 390 and Part 6B Boxes 780–786), Shared-Use Equipment (Line 504 and Part 6C Boxes 788–796), and equipment leases, maintain contemporaneous machine-hour logbooks proving ≥90% (ASA) or >50% (primary) SR&ED operating time across the full taxation year, verify that SUE and capital ITC claims involve new (not used) equipment under Regulation 2902(b), and document acquisition intent to defeat Prescribed Depreciable Property (PDP) challenges under Regulation 2900(11).

Segregate Subcontractors and File Non-Arm's Length Agreements (Forms T1145 & T1146): Separate arm's-length Canadian taxable supplier SR&ED contracts (claimed at 80% for ITC) from non-arm's length contracts (ineligible for ITC unless transferred via Form T1146 by the transferor's T2 filing-due date) and third-party payments (Form T1263).

Enforce the 180-Day Unpaid Amount Cutoff: Review accrued bonuses, wages, and contractor payables 180 days after fiscal year-end to identify any unpaid wages under subsection 78(4) and unpaid current/contract expenses under subsection 127(26).

Optimize Provincial Credits and Apply Project-by-Project Assistance Grinding: For Québec operations, transition from legacy R&D credits to the CRIC (Form RD-1029.8.CR-T) for tax years beginning after March 25, 2025, capturing newly eligible pre-commercialization (regulatory validation and product design) and capital equipment costs while computing the exclusion threshold (greater of $50,000 or the employee BPA of $18,952 per full-time eligible employee in 2026). For Ontario, BC, and Alberta operations, apply the updated post-Bill C-15 capital and current expenditure rules and grind federal Form T661 (Lines 513/514) by all provincial credits and NRC IRAP / SIF grants.

Calendar the Absolute 18-Month Statutory Filing Bar and Complete Part 9 Disclosures: Ensure Form T661 (with complete Part 2 descriptions for all claimed projects) and Schedule T2SCH31 are filed well ahead of the non-extendable 18-month corporate deadline under subsections 37(11), 127(9)(m), and 220(2.2), and verify complete Part 9 claim preparer disclosures to avoid the $1,000 joint-and-several penalty.
